source: AAA gasprices.aaa.com national average — $3.872 on Monday July 13, 2026 (Day 136), up from $3.84 (July 9) and $3.804 (July 5) as the war reignited; EIA's weekly read printed $3.855 (July 13). The US-Iran ceasefire COLLAPSED in this window: Iran fired on three Hormuz-area tankers July 7, Trump declared the ceasefire 'over' July 8, CENTCOM ran five-plus strike waves against 300+ Iranian targets July 7-14, and the US naval blockade of Iranian ports was reimposed effective July 14 (20:00 GMT). Brent settled +9.59% at $83.30 on July 13 — its biggest daily percentage gain since May 2020 and highest settlement since June 12 (Reuters) — with WTI at $78.14; both traded higher intraday July 14 (~$85 / ~$80). Pump prices lag crude by 2-3 weeks, so further increases are likely if the blockade and tanker attacks sustain Brent above $80. Still ~$0.88/gal above the $2.99 Feb 28 baseline (~30% higher). The wartime peak was ~$4.56/gal (May 21), below AAA's nominal record of $5.016 (June 14, 2022). Moody's Analytics (NPR, mid-June) estimated at least $132 billion in combined US consumer and taxpayer costs — now a stale undercount that predates the July escalation.
